# ai-operant-box

> LLM-as-subject simulator for OperantKit: a large language model or a numerical agent is the organism in a discrete-time operant chamber, sensing a discriminative stimulus, emitting a response, and receiving a consequence on every step under CRF, FI, Fleshler-Hoffman VI / VR, RI / RR, or a dyadic interdependent schedule.

ai-operant-box is part of OperantKit, a set of Python/Rust packages for designing and running operant and respondent conditioning experiments (reinforcement schedules, session recording, analysis). Use it to study whether and how an LLM's responding comes under the control of reinforcement contingencies, with the same chamber, schedules, and simulated clock as numerical baseline subjects, instead of hand-writing a prompt loop that counts "presses".

## Install

From a clone (the core package needs only NumPy):

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e .
```

Optional extras: `llm` (Anthropic SDK for `LLMSubject`), `viz` (session-analyzer, matplotlib, SciPy), `canonical` (experiment-core and session-recorder for OKL v1 logs).

## Minimal example

```python
import random

from ai_operant_box.agent.scallop_agent import ScallopingAgent
from ai_operant_box.chamber.environment import OperantBox
from ai_operant_box.chamber.schedule import FixedInterval

random.seed(42)
agent = ScallopingAgent(k=0.005)
box = OperantBox(subject=agent, schedule=FixedInterval(30.0))
for _ in range(600):
    agent.update_time(1.0)
    box.step(1.0)
print(len(box.records), sum(r.is_reinforced for r in box.records))
# 422 20
```

The clock is simulated, so the run needs no API key and prints the same numbers every time.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/OperantKit/ai-operant-box/blob/main/README.md): install, 30-second example, why not to hand-roll a chamber, optional extras
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OperantKit/ai-operant-box/blob/main/AGENTS.md): when to use this package and what not to do

## Related packages

- [experiment-core](https://github.com/OperantKit/experiment-core): canonical session events that `canonical_sink` maps the native event stream into
- [session-recorder](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-recorder): OKL v1 log writer and reader
- [session-analyzer](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-analyzer): cumulative records, statistics, and model fitting
- [contingency-py](https://github.com/OperantKit/contingency-py): the OperantKit schedule engine for real sessions (this package does not import it; its schedules are implemented here)
- [operantkit-cli](https://github.com/OperantKit/operantkit-cli): run one contingency-dsl schedule against a virtual Poisson subject and write an OKL v1 log
- [operantkit-mcp](https://github.com/OperantKit/operantkit-mcp): MCP server that lets an AI assistant check and simulate contingency-dsl schedules
